recommendations.title: Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes Screening
recommendations.recommendation_text: Screen for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity. Offer or refer patients with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: If you are 35–70 years old with overweight or obesity, USPSTF recommends diabetes screening. Talk to your doctor about a fasting glucose or A1c test.

recommendations.title: Colorectal Cancer Screening
recommendations.recommendation_text: Screen for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years. The decision to screen adults aged 76 to 85 years should be individualized.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: Adults 45–75 should be screened for colorectal cancer. Options include colonoscopy every 10 years, stool DNA testing (Cologuard) every 1–3 years, or annual stool blood tests. Ask your doctor which is right for you.

recommendations.title: Breast Cancer Screening (Mammography)
recommendations.recommendation_text: Screen for breast cancer with mammography every 2 years for women aged 40 to 74 years.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: Women 40–74 should get a mammogram every 2 years. Talk to your doctor about when to start and how often based on your personal risk.

recommendations.title: Cervical Cancer Screening
recommendations.recommendation_text: Screen for cervical cancer every 3 years with cervical cytology alone (Pap smear) in women aged 21 to 65. For women 30–65, screening every 5 years with hrHPV testing alone or co-testing is also acceptable.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: Women 21–65 should be screened for cervical cancer. Ages 21–29: Pap smear every 3 years. Ages 30–65: Pap smear every 3 years, or HPV test every 5 years, or both together every 5 years.

recommendations.title: Lung Cancer Screening (Low-Dose CT)
recommendations.recommendation_text: Annual low-dose CT scan for lung cancer screening in adults aged 50–80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: If you're 50–80, have smoked heavily for many years, and currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years, ask your doctor about annual low-dose CT lung cancer screening.

recommendations.title: Hypertension in Adults: Screening
recommendations.recommendation_text: Screen for hypertension in adults 18 years or older. Obtain measurements outside of the clinical setting for diagnostic confirmation before starting treatment.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: All adults should have their blood pressure checked regularly. If it's elevated, home or ambulatory monitoring is recommended before starting treatment.

recommendations.title: Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Screening
recommendations.recommendation_text: Screen for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults aged 18 to 79 years.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: Adults 18–79 should be screened for hepatitis C at least once. If you have ongoing risk factors, more frequent screening may be recommended.

recommendations.title: Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Screening
recommendations.recommendation_text: Screen for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adolescents and adults at increased risk for infection.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: Those at increased risk for hepatitis B — including people born in countries with high HBV prevalence (including South Korea, China, and Southeast Asia) — should be screened.

recommendations.title: A1c Monitoring in Diabetes
recommendations.recommendation_text: A1c should be measured at least twice yearly in patients meeting treatment goals and quarterly in patients not meeting goals or after therapy change.
recommendations.patient_facing_summary: If you have diabetes, your A1c should be checked at least twice a year if controlled, and every 3 months if not at goal or after a medication change.
